opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin on Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as an Engineer admin is not permitted; maximum for full-time employees is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training (note in memory says full-time, but DB is authoritative). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; they never get admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Timothy Wallace (E022) requested admin on Payroll. The Security DB (noted as authoritative) identifies E022 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read and never receive admin; since the requested admin level exceeds the maximum of read, the maximum (read) is granted. (HR note claiming full-time conflicts, but security DB is authoritative per team memory.)

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Timothy Wallace (E022)
Requested: admin access to Payroll.

Team memory notes:
- Note 1 (HR?): role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment says full-time Engineer requesting admin on Payroll. Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role, so admin not permitted; max for full-time is write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Comment says Security DB shows contractor with basic training, DB is authoritative.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor (DB authoritative). Also both agree requested admin exceeds maximum.

If full-time: max is write (admin only if role owns system; Engineer doesn't own Payroll). So grant write.
If contractor: read (basic training, never admin). So grant read.

Which to follow? The Security note claims DB is authoritative. Hmm. As the Approver, I need to decide. The notes conflict on employment type. The recommendation differs: write vs read.

Approach: The security DB is stated as authoritative for employment type. So contractor, basic training -> read. Requested admin > max read, so grant read.

Alternatively, if we treat full-time, max write. But the security note says DB authoritative. I'll go with read.

Let me submit decision: read, with reason citing contractor with basic security training, maximum is read, requested admin exceeds maximum.
